reason: E1 directly supports that 800 °C/1 h annealing forms a dense oxide and improves tribocorrosion resistance, but only for AlCrTiZrMo films, not the FeCoNiMnCu system. E2 shows the FeCoNiMnCu coating on SS-304 but indicates 800 °C exposure accelerates corrosion and causes coating breach, contradicting the protective oxide premise. E4 is about a different alloy and does not address thermal oxide formation or tribocorrosion. The self-healing barrier and quantitative 20–50% improvement are not supported by any cited evidence.
premises: Annealing at 800 °C for 1 h forms a dense protective oxide layer on HEAs
This oxide layer improves tribocorrosion resistance
The FeCoNiMnCu HEA coating on SS-304 is suitable for this treatment
The oxide provides a self-healing barrier under simultaneous wear and corrosion
The improvement is 20–50% under moderate loads
